date_note: Yonhap (19 Nov) and Dailysecu (20 Nov) say the ministry announced the plan on 19 November; pre-legislative notice starts 20 November.
title: South Korea plans higher minimum penalty for civil servants who leak personal information
impact: Proposed rule change; not yet in force.
summary: South Korea's Ministry of Personnel Management said on 19 November it will put an amendment to the enforcement rules of the civil servant disciplinary code out for pre-legislative notice from 20 November, Yonhap and Dailysecu report. It would raise the minimum penalty for leaking secrets or personal information from reprimand to pay reduction and let supervisors and non-political agency heads be held accountable. No effective date is stated.
plain: South Korea proposes tougher minimum discipline, a pay cut, for civil servants who leak personal data, and for bosses who neglect oversight.
exec: Public-sector data leaks in Korea may carry heavier discipline, including for agency heads, once the rule takes effect.

validation.note: Two independent publishers read: Dailysecu (20 Nov) and Yonhap News (19 Nov, republished on koreancenter.or.kr), both state the 19 November announcement, the reprimand-to-pay-reduction minimum, supervisor and non-political agency-head accountability and the 20 November pre-legislative notice. The ministry's own notice was not read; neither page gives a comment deadline or effective date.
